messages:
incident-bot: Paging on-call: detected sustained p95/p99 latency spike on streaming endpoints (SSE and websocket). Alerts: streaming-tail_latency.p95 > 600ms for 3m, streaming-tail_latency.p99 > 2s for 2m. Possible proxy timeouts and slow consumer buildup. Auto-escalation to #incidents.

oncall-amy: I'm on it. First pass: is this global or region-specific?

ben_sre: Seeing it in us-west-2 + eu-west-1. grafana: https://grafana.redwood/sys/streaming?panel=tail_latency (link). p95 jumped from ~120ms->700ms, p99 to ~3.6s.

carla_prod: Customers impacted: 4 high-traffic integrations (chat widgets) reported partial streaming stalls and reconnects. Error reports show long chunk gaps, clients timing out. No full outage.

dmitri_infra: Logs from edge-proxy show repeated "write timeout" and "client slow consumer" warnings around the same window. Example:```
[2026-03-14T22:13:02Z] WARN proxy[conn=44]: write timeout to 10.1.3.45: broken pipe
[2026-03-14T22:13:02Z] WARN proxy: client buffer backlog size=12MB
[2026-03-14T22:13:03Z] ERROR stream-handler: stalled chunk flush for request_id=req-9c3b
```

oncall-amy: Looks like slow consumers at the proxy/backpressure layer. Quick mitigations?

ben_sre: Short-term: increase proxy upstream timeout from 60s -> 90s to avoid premature resets, and enable more aggressive chunk flushing so one slow client doesn't block others. I've got a patch ready for the proxy conf. Applying to canary.

carla_prod: Can we also bounce the streaming worker on host pool-a? We see some workers with high epoll wait times. Might be connection table leaking.

ben_sre: Agree. I'll recycle 2 nodes in pool-a now (rolling) and monitor. Command I'm running: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/streaming-runtime -n prod --field-selector=spec.nodeName=pool-a`

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Started canary update to proxy-config v2026-03-14-45 on proxy-usw-1.

pm_jane: Customer comms: only surface-level reports from support so far. No major SLAs breached yet but p99 > 3s is concerning. Please include list of affected customers and expected ETA for full mitigation.

ben_sre: Initial customer impact: integrations A,B,C,D (IDs: 86, 234, 901, 114) show >5% of streaming sessions with stalls >5s during the spike. Sending opt-in monitoring hooks to PMs.

oncall-amy: Canary proxy config applied and rolling restart started. Watching metrics. If p99 drops within 2 cycles (5m) we'll promote.

(5 minutes pass)

ben_sre: Canary looks good: p95 down to ~180ms, p99 down to ~650ms in canary's region. Promoting to all proxies.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Proxy-config v2026-03-14-45 promoted to 6/6 proxies.

carla_prod: Node restarts completed on pool-a. Epoll wait improved on restarted workers. No crash loops.

dmitri_infra: Observability notes: root cause hypothesis: a recent client change increased per-connection buffer retention (large JSON deltas), combined with default proxy write behavior causing head-of-line stalls. When one consumer slowed, the proxy backlog prevented timely chunk flushes to other clients. Proxy would then hit socket write timeouts and reset, forcing reconnects.

oncall-amy: Actions taken so far: 1) Proxy timeout bump + chunk-flush tweak (done) 2) Rolling restart of streaming runtime in affected pool (done) 3) Canary verification and full promotion (done) 4) Increased keepalive interval for websocket -> 30s for earlier heartbeat detect (done)

oncall-amy: Short-term mitigations to keep: keepalive change and proxy flush tuning. Recommend follow-ups for infra and product.

pm_jane: For customers: draft message: "We observed elevated streaming latency between 22:10-22:25 UTC affecting some streaming sessions. We mitigated via configuration changes and rolling restarts; latency now back to normal. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with technical details." Approve? :thumbsup:

carla_prod: :thumbsup: send it. Add which customers we identified.

ben_sre: Follow-up items / owners: - Root cause RCA (dmitri_infra) - Add backpressure metrics to dashboards (ben_sre) - API contract check with SDK team about chunk sizing (carla_prod) - Add automated detection/auto-shed policy for slow consumers to avoid head-of-line blocking (oncall-amy)

dmitri_infra: Early RCA notes: reproduce path locally by simulating a slow consumer that does not read from socket; observe proxy backlog growth and stalls. Need to validate whether kernel socket buffer tuning could help and whether proxy should stream partial flushes more frequently.

oncall-amy: Handoff to next on-call @ben_sre in ~30m. Current status: stable, p95/p99 within SLOs (p95 ~150-200ms, p99 <700ms), no new customer reports. Keep mitigations in place until RCA complete.

ben_sre: Taking handoff. I'll keep the runbook open and coordinate RCA. Leaving a pinned checklist in #incidents.

incident-bot: Incident severity: SEV3 -> downgraded. Handoff complete.

pm_jane: Thanks all — follow up with timeline and RCA when ready.

carla_prod: Logged support cases with affected customers and set follow-up calls.

ben_sre: Quick note for RCA: include metric stanza: `streaming.proxy.backlog_bytes`, `streaming.conn.write_timeouts`, `streaming.client.read_rate` and link to replay logs (s3://prod-logs/streaming/2026-03-14/22/).

oncall-amy: Closing thread for now. If anything regresses, re-open or @page. :white_check_mark:
